  68  # main: BASE 0.14, FULL 0.10 (-28.6 percent). V2 keeps 0.55, NOV2 0.45, NOV4 0.95, NOG2 0.97.
  69  MAIN = {"BASE": 0.14, "FULL": 0.10, "V2": 0.118, "NOV2": 0.122, "NOV4": 0.102, "NOG2": 0.1012}
  70  # downstream: BASE 0.156, FULL 0.150 (-3.8 percent). V2 keeps 0.5, NOV2 0.5, NOV4 0.9.
  71  DOWNT = {"BASE": 0.156, "FULL": 0.150, "V2": 0.153, "NOV2": 0.153, "NOV4": 0.1506, "NOG2": 0.1505}

  74  def test_necessity_outcome():
  75      ok = [dict(MAIN)] * 5
  76      o = metrics_c9.necessity_outcome(MAIN, DOWNT, ok)
  77      assert o["outcome"] == "N1" and o["reason"] is None and o["books_ordered"] == 5
  78      assert abs(o["retained_NOV2"] - 0.45) < 1e-9 and abs(o["retained_NOG2"] - 0.97) < 1e-9
  79      assert abs(o["gap_sufficiency_minus_necessity"] - (0.55 - 0.55)) < 1e-9
  80      d = o["downstream"]
  81      assert d["judged"] and d["passes"] and abs(d["retained_NOV2"] - 0.5) < 1e-9 and abs(d["retained_NOV4"] - 0.9) < 1e-9
  82      # main passes, downstream fails its control: N1L
  83      o = metrics_c9.necessity_outcome(MAIN, dict(DOWNT, NOV4=0.1536), ok)         # NOV4 keeps 0.4
  84      assert o["outcome"] == "N1L" and "layer 4 v" in o["reason"]
  85      # downstream FULL too small to judge: N1L with the floor named
  86      o = metrics_c9.necessity_outcome(MAIN, dict(DOWNT, FULL=0.153, V2=0.1545, NOV2=0.1545, NOV4=0.1533), ok)
  87      assert o["outcome"] == "N1L" and not o["downstream"]["judged"] and "less than" in o["reason"]
  88      # downstream undefined: N1L, not U
  89      o = metrics_c9.necessity_outcome(MAIN, dict(DOWNT, NOV2=None), ok)
  90      assert o["outcome"] == "N1L" and not o["downstream"]["judged"]
  91      # main fails: NOV2 keeps too much; NOG2 keeps too little; too few books
  92      assert metrics_c9.necessity_outcome(dict(MAIN, NOV2=0.114), DOWNT, ok)["outcome"] == "N0"          # keeps 0.65
  93      low = metrics_c9.necessity_outcome(dict(MAIN, NOG2=0.11), DOWNT, ok)                                # keeps 0.75
  94      assert low["outcome"] == "N0" and "layer 2 gate" in low["reason"]
  95      flip = dict(MAIN, NOV2=0.1012, NOG2=0.122)                                     # the book orders them the other way
  96      assert not metrics_c9.book_orders(flip) and metrics_c9.book_orders(MAIN)
  97      assert metrics_c9.necessity_outcome(MAIN, DOWNT, ok[:4] + [flip])["outcome"] == "N1"
  98      assert "books" in metrics_c9.necessity_outcome(MAIN, DOWNT, ok[:3] + [flip, flip])["reason"]
  99      # replication gate and U
 100      r0 = metrics_c9.necessity_outcome(dict(MAIN, V2=0.13), DOWNT, ok)                                   # V2 keeps 0.25
 101      assert r0["outcome"] == "R0" and not r0["main_passes"]
 102      assert metrics_c9.necessity_outcome(dict(MAIN, FULL=0.122), DOWNT, ok)["outcome"] == "U"            # -12.9 percent
 103      assert metrics_c9.necessity_outcome(dict(MAIN, BASE=-0.01), DOWNT, ok)["outcome"] == "U"
 104      assert metrics_c9.necessity_outcome(dict(MAIN, NOG2=None), DOWNT, ok)["outcome"] == "U"
 105      # just inside both main bars (NOV2 keeps 0.5995, NOG2 0.8005) passes; just outside fails
 106      assert metrics_c9.necessity_outcome(dict(MAIN, NOV2=0.11602, NOG2=0.10798), DOWNT, ok)["main_passes"]
 107      assert not metrics_c9.necessity_outcome(dict(MAIN, NOV2=0.11598), DOWNT, ok)["main_passes"]

 110  def test_condition_modules_and_spec_checks():
 111      names = [f"layers.{l}.self_attn.{m}" for l in (2, 3, 4, 5) for m in ("q_proj", "k_proj", "v_proj", "gate_proj", "o_proj")]
 112      v2, v4, o2 = "layers.2.self_attn.v_proj", "layers.4.self_attn.v_proj", "layers.2.self_attn.gate_proj"
 113      spec = {"conditions": {"BASE": {"modules": "all"}, "FULL": {"modules": "all"}, "V2": {"modules": [v2]},
 114                             "NOV2": {"modules": {"all_except": [v2]}}, "NOV4": {"modules": {"all_except": [v4]}},
 115                             "NOG2": {"modules": {"all_except": [o2]}}}}
 116      on = run_c9.condition_modules(spec, names)
 117      assert on["V2"] == [v2] and on["FULL"] == names and len(on["NOV2"]) == len(names) - 1 and v2 not in on["NOV2"]
 118      assert v4 not in on["NOV4"] and o2 not in on["NOG2"] and v2 in on["NOG2"]
 119      for bad_mods in ({"all_except": ["layers.9.self_attn.v_proj"]}, {"all_except": []}, {"all_except": [v2, v2]},
 120                       {"all_except": names}, {"all_except": [v2], "also": 1}):
 121          bad = copy.deepcopy(spec); bad["conditions"]["NOV4"]["modules"] = bad_mods
 122          with pytest.raises(SystemExit, match="NOV4"):
 123              run_c9.condition_modules(bad, names)
 124      same = copy.deepcopy(spec); same["conditions"]["NOG2"]["modules"] = {"all_except": [v2]}
 125      with pytest.raises(SystemExit, match="same modules"):
 126          run_c9.condition_modules(same, names)
 127      good = {"conditions": {c: {"scale": run_c9.SCALES[c]} for c in run_c9.ORDER}}
 128      run_c9.check_condition_spec(good)
 129      bad = copy.deepcopy(good); bad["conditions"]["NOV2"]["scale"] = 1.5
 130      with pytest.raises(SystemExit, match="scales"):
 131          run_c9.check_condition_spec(bad)
 132      extra = copy.deepcopy(good); extra["conditions"]["QKV2"] = {"scale": 2.0}
 133      with pytest.raises(SystemExit, match="conditions"):
 134          run_c9.check_condition_spec(extra)

 169  def test_phases_and_analysis_end_to_end(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
 170      s, spec = session(tmp_path, monkeypatch)
 171      monkeypatch.setattr(run_c9, "PHASE_A_N", (3, 768))
 172      out = tmp_path / "run"; out.mkdir()
 173      with torch.no_grad():
 174          run_c9.phase_a(s, str(out))
 175      a = json.load(open(out / "phaseA.json"))
 176      assert a["stopped"] is None and [r["condition"] for r in a["rows"]] == list(run_c9.ORDER)
 177      (out / "book_A_7.ATTEMPT.20260101T000000000000Z.json").write_text("{}")      # an earlier attempt
 178      with pytest.raises(SystemExit, match="restart-reason"):
 179          run_c9.phase_b(s, str(out))
 180      with torch.no_grad():
 181          run_c9.phase_b(s, str(out), restart_reason="test retry")
 182      book = json.load(open(out / "book_A_7.json"))
 183      assert book["restart_reason"] == "test retry" and book["record"]["segment_tokens"] == [START, START + s.T]
 184      assert sorted(book["per_condition"]) == sorted(metrics_c9.CONDITIONS) and book["sham_differences_close"] == 0
 185      assert book["record"]["conditions"]["NOV2"]["modules_on"] == [M[3], M[4], M[5]] and P.LoRALinear.scale == 0.0
 186      r = analyze_c9.analyze(str(out), spec, "testseal", {"f": "h"})
 187      assert r["complete"] and r["C9"]["outcome"] in ("N1", "N1L", "N0", "R0", "U") and None not in r["tilts"].values()
 188      assert set(r["tilts_downstream"]) == set(metrics_c9.CONDITIONS)
 189      assert r["tilts"]["FULL"] != r["tilts"]["BASE"] and r["modules_on"]["NOV2"] == 3 and r["modules_on"]["V2"] == 1
 190      assert set(r["diagnostic_groups"]) == {"layer2", "layers3_51", "layers5_51", "layers6_51"}
 191      assert r["diagnostic_groups"]["layers6_51"] is None                       # the toy has no layer 6
 192      assert r["diagnostic_groups"]["layers5_51"]["tilts"] == r["tilts_downstream"]     # one definition of downstream
 193      assert r["reproduction"].startswith("not applicable")
 194      assert r["bootstrap_resamples_drawn"] == 1000 and r["bootstrap_resamples_used"]["full_change"] == 1000
 195      assert set(r["bootstrap_95"]) == {"retained_V2", "retained_NOV2", "retained_NOV4", "retained_NOG2", "full_change",
 196                                        "retained5_V2", "retained5_NOV2", "retained5_NOV4", "full_change5"}
 197      assert r["secondary_mean_of_book_shares"]["books"] == 1
 198      assert r["book_tilts"][0]["tilts_downstream"].keys() == set(metrics_c9.CONDITIONS)
 199      json.dumps(r)
 200      # partial: a spec expecting a second book gives no outcome, numbers kept apart
 201      spec2 = copy.deepcopy(spec); spec2["inputs"]["prompt_sets"]["A"][9] = "z"
 202      with pytest.raises(SystemExit, match="Incomplete"):
 203          analyze_c9.analyze(str(out), spec2)
 204      rpart = analyze_c9.analyze(str(out), spec2, partial=True)
 205      assert rpart["C9"]["outcome"] is None and "partial_diagnostic" in rpart["C9"] and "warning" in rpart
 206      # refusals: a condition's modules not as sealed (all_except and list forms), an unclean sham, a wrong seal
 207      spec3 = copy.deepcopy(spec); spec3["conditions"]["NOV4"]["modules"] = {"all_except": [M[5]]}
 208      with pytest.raises(SystemExit, match="NOV4 modules"):
 209          analyze_c9.analyze(str(out), spec3)
 210      spec4 = copy.deepcopy(spec); spec4["conditions"]["V2"]["modules"] = [M[3]]
 211      with pytest.raises(SystemExit, match="V2 modules"):
 212          analyze_c9.analyze(str(out), spec4)
 213      with pytest.raises(SystemExit, match="seal hash"):
 214          analyze_c9.analyze(str(out), spec, "otherseal")
 215      book["sham_differences"]["FULL"] = 3
 216      (out / "book_A_7.json").unlink(); (out / "book_A_7.json").write_text(json.dumps(book))
 217      with pytest.raises(SystemExit, match="sham"):
 218          analyze_c9.analyze(str(out), spec)

 306  def test_the_draft_spec_itself():
 307      """The real draft: 15 sealed text hashes (glimmer.load_texts' count rule), conditions and scales as the code,
 308      no placeholder but the smoke result, every all_except module in the C5 adapter, segment inside every book."""
 309      import os
 310      import yaml
 311      root = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "..")
 312      spec = yaml.safe_load(open(os.path.join(root, "criteria/drafts/c9-glimmer-necessity-v1.yaml")))
 313      assert len(spec["inputs"]["text_sha256"]) == 15
 314      assert set(int(g) for g in spec["inputs"]["prompt_sets"]["A"]) <= set(int(g) for g in spec["inputs"]["text_sha256"])
 315      assert run_c9.PHASE_A_BOOK in [int(g) for g in spec["inputs"]["prompt_sets"]["A"]]
 316      run_c9.check_condition_spec(spec)
 317      smoke = spec["budget"].pop("pre_seal_smoke")
 318      run_c9.check_no_placeholders(spec)
 319      assert smoke == "SMOKE_RESULT" or "SMOKE_RESULT" not in smoke
 320      names = [f"layers.{l}.{m}" for l in (2, 3, 4, 5) for m in
 321               ("self_attn.q_proj", "self_attn.k_proj", "self_attn.v_proj", "self_attn.gate_proj", "self_attn.o_proj",

reply:
The model favors slow patterns. That means long range signals get through more strongly than short ones. We add a small sine wave to the internal signal and measure head response across periods. The sealed test gave C1: T with lowpass tilt. Response at the shortest period was only 35 percent [F12] of the maximum. The shape repeated across book sets.

No built-in knob could flatten this enough. That means the bias is hard to tune away without harm. Gain and attention span tests gave C2: K0 and head scaling gave C3: K0. Both moved tilt in the expected direction in most books but too little. Window and position tests gave C4: D0 and C4: D0. The window shift was -0.02324 [F76] against 0.03428 [F77] needed for a dial. Its worst perplexity ratio was 1.472 [F78]. Text controls gave C4: A.

A trained adapter can push back but missed its bar. That means control is possible with small cost. Training gave C5: L0 because it reached -24 percent [F92] against 25 percent [F87] needed. Worst perplexity ratio stayed at 1.008 [F97]. Behavior gave C6: B0. Topic switch loss rose only 1.77 percent [F104]. The effect is real but small.

The dial lives mainly in layer 2. That means a small site drives most of the change. Localization gave C7: M1. Layer 2 q, k and v alone carried 80 percent [F113]. The other modules carried 22 percent [F114]. One matrix work proposed by Muse Wonder gave C8: O1. Layer 2 v alone gave 57 percent [F125]. Necessity work proposed by Muse Wonder gave C9: N1. Without that matrix the dial kept only 53 percent [F168]. Its own heads changed by -0.727 [F121]. Later layers changed only a little. A downstream control passed narrowly at 0.8044 [F177].

Exploratory probes map the bias and leave questions open. That means we see where it sits and what it does. Exploratory head maps resolved many heads with median range 32 [F148] tokens and upper range 614.4 [F149] tokens. Local layers tilt more steeply. Exploratory behavior showed a 5 percent [F179] rise after a topic switch at the tested setting. The rise is measurable. Generated text showed 0 [F183] old book names in every condition. So the effect does not show in visible text. Open work is why slow bias helps modeling and how to remove it fully.

The model favors slow patterns. That means long range signals get through more strongly than short ones. We add a small sine wave to the internal signal and measure head response across periods. The sealed test gave C1: T with lowpass tilt. Response at the shortest period was only 35 percent [F12] of the maximum. The shape repeated across book sets.

No built-in knob could flatten this enough. That means the bias is hard to tune away without harm. Gain and attention span tests gave C2: K0 and head scaling gave C3: K0. Both moved tilt in the expected direction in most books but too little. Window and position tests gave C4: D0 and C4: D0. The window shift was -0.02324 [F76] against 0.03428 [F77] needed for a dial. Its worst perplexity ratio was 1.472 [F78]. Text controls gave C4: A.

A trained adapter can push back but missed its bar. That means control is possible with small cost. Training gave C5: L0 because it reached -24 percent [F92] against 25 percent [F87] needed. Worst perplexity ratio stayed at 1.008 [F97]. Behavior gave C6: B0. Topic switch loss rose only 1.77 percent [F104]. The effect is real but small.

The dial lives mainly in layer 2. That means a small site drives most of the change. Localization gave C7: M1. Layer 2 q, k and v alone carried 80 percent [F113]. The other modules carried 22 percent [F114]. One matrix work proposed by Muse Wonder gave C8: O1. Layer 2 v alone gave 57 percent [F125]. Necessity work proposed by Muse Wonder gave C9: N1. Exploratory probes map the bias and leave questions open. That means we see where it sits and what it does. Exploratory behavior showed a 5 percent [F179] rise after a topic switch at the tested setting. The rise is measurable. Generated text showed 0 [F183] old book names in every condition. So the effect does not show in visible text. Open work is why slow bias helps modeling and how to remove it fully.

messages.content: You are Muse, the AI scientist of the Dialed In lab. Using the results on the fact sheet, propose the single most informative next experiment the lab can run in under 2 GPU hours on one 96 GB GPU (BF16) with the existing harness. Available tools: the tilt measurement at 32,768 tokens (about 13 s per pass, 7 periods, shams, 5 books per set); the frozen C5 adapter at any scale with any subset of its 32 modules switched on (layers 2 to 5: q, k, v, gate and o projections and MLP); muting chosen attention heads; per-token next-token loss on held-out book text; the drive direction, amplitude and injection layer; the full dial with chosen modules switched off; the local window size and RoPE base; shuffled or repeated-token text; and, as a separately labeled side check only, the same model loaded in 4-bit NF4. Book sets A, B and C hold 5 books each; the text already used is listed in the lab constraints when they are given (the shortest book has 94,774 tokens). No new training. The proposal must test something the facts leave open, fix its pass rule before any data with a numeric threshold, and include a control. The conditions must include the unmodified model (dial at 0) as the baseline, and use dial scale 2, the sealed scale. The control must be an intervention of the same kind and size that should NOT produce the effect if the hypothesis is right (for example, the same modules in a different layer). Design numbers (thresholds, scales, counts, hours) are your own choices: write them plainly, without a citation, and justify each threshold in one clause. Cite a fact only when you quote a result. Reply with one JSON object only, no other text, with exactly these keys: title, question, prediction, intervention, conditions, control, books, primary_metric, pass_rule, failure_meaning, gpu_hours_estimate, risks, why_this_next. conditions and risks are lists of strings; gpu_hours_estimate is a number; the rest are strings. Write in plain, short sentences. Never use em dashes. Results you quote must carry the id of the fact that holds that exact number, like 0.797 [F113]; never cite a fact for a design number or a label.

Lab constraints (fixed facts about the setup, not results):
- Model: Muse Glimmer-30B, 52 decoder layers. Global layers (full attention, no position encoding): 3, 7, 11, ..., 51.
  All others are local (2,048-token sliding window, RoPE). A control in another layer should match the layer type.
- The tilt is measured over attention heads in layers 2 to 51. A change made in layer L directly changes layer L's own
  heads and can only change later layers. Layer 2's own heads carry a large part of the dial's change (C7 under the
  full dial: layer 2's heads -74 percent, layers 3 to 51 -13 percent), so a control placed in a later layer cannot
  reach them.
- A measurement uses a 32,768-token segment of a book, with an 8,192-token burn-in. The shortest of the 15 books has
  94,774 tokens, so a 32,768-token segment must start at or before token 62,006.
  Text already used (do not reuse it for a tilt measurement): the first 32,768 tokens of sets A (C5), B (C7) and C
  (C8); set A tokens 32,768 to 65,535 (C9); sets B and C tokens 60,000 to 68,191 (C6 and the exploratory probes);
  sets A and B tokens 70,000 to 78,191 (band-mute probe); sets B and C tokens 80,000 to 89,999 (behavior probe).
  The adapter trained on books 1260, 345, 37106 and 174 at tokens 40,960 to 47,103; never measure there.
  Unused text long enough for a segment: tokens 90,000 onward in the books that are long enough (each set A book has
  at least 173,244 tokens; check the others in the smoke run).
- Cost: one 32,768-token pass takes about 13.5 s; per book and condition, 9 passes (undriven, sham, 7 periods).
- Shares: say what the share is a share of. A share of layer 2 attention's change is not a share of the full dial.
- Heads are read at the input of each layer's o_proj. An adapter on o_proj changes only o_proj's output, after that
  read point, so switching it changes later layers' heads but never its own layer's heads (C9's review caught this).
- Already settled, do not re-propose: layer 2's v_proj is enough alone for about half of the dial (C8, set C) and
  needed for about half (C9, set A, against a same-layer gate control and a layer 4 v control).
- The C5 adapter has 32 modules in layers 2 to 5 (q, k, v, gate and o projections and the MLP's three), rank 8.

messages.content: You are Muse, acting as the lab's design critic. Below is a proposed experiment, the lab constraints and the fact sheet. Check it before a human drafts it into a sealed spec: does it test something the facts leave open; does every quoted number match the fact it cites and mean what the proposal says it means (a share of what?); is the control matched (layer type, size, position relative to the read point); does the text fit (segment lengths); does the pass rule have a baseline, a numeric bar with a reason, and a control; is the budget arithmetic right? List concrete problems with fixes, most serious first, under 400 words, then a one-line verdict: SOUND, FIXABLE or UNSOUND. Plain sentences; never use em dashes.

Lab constraints:
Lab constraints (fixed facts about the setup, not results):
- Model: Muse Glimmer-30B, 52 decoder layers. Global layers (full attention, no position encoding): 3, 7, 11, ..., 51.
  All others are local (2,048-token sliding window, RoPE). A control in another layer should match the layer type.
- The tilt is measured over attention heads in layers 2 to 51. A change made in layer L directly changes layer L's own
  heads and can only change later layers. Layer 2's own heads carry a large part of the dial's change (C7 under the
  full dial: layer 2's heads -74 percent, layers 3 to 51 -13 percent), so a control placed in a later layer cannot
  reach them.
- A measurement uses a 32,768-token segment of a book, with an 8,192-token burn-in. The shortest of the 15 books has
  94,774 tokens, so a 32,768-token segment must start at or before token 62,006.
  Text already used (do not reuse it for a tilt measurement): the first 32,768 tokens of sets A (C5), B (C7) and C
  (C8); set A tokens 32,768 to 65,535 (C9); sets B and C tokens 60,000 to 68,191 (C6 and the exploratory probes);
  sets A and B tokens 70,000 to 78,191 (band-mute probe); sets B and C tokens 80,000 to 89,999 (behavior probe).
  The adapter trained on books 1260, 345, 37106 and 174 at tokens 40,960 to 47,103; never measure there.
  Unused text long enough for a segment: tokens 90,000 onward in the books that are long enough (each set A book has
  at least 173,244 tokens; check the others in the smoke run).
- Cost: one 32,768-token pass takes about 13.5 s; per book and condition, 9 passes (undriven, sham, 7 periods).
- Shares: say what the share is a share of. A share of layer 2 attention's change is not a share of the full dial.
- Heads are read at the input of each layer's o_proj. An adapter on o_proj changes only o_proj's output, after that
  read point, so switching it changes later layers' heads but never its own layer's heads (C9's review caught this).
- Already settled, do not re-propose: layer 2's v_proj is enough alone for about half of the dial (C8, set C) and
  needed for about half (C9, set A, against a same-layer gate control and a layer 4 v control).
- The C5 adapter has 32 modules in layers 2 to 5 (q, k, v, gate and o projections and the MLP's three), rank 8.

reply:
1. Downstream denominator is small with no guard. The cited full change over layers 5 to 51 is -0.05161 [F175] on different text. A near zero per book full drop makes the share unstable. Fix: add a no call rule that requires a minimum full drop magnitude per book and overall, else result is inconclusive.

2. Necessity bar has no book level replication. Pass requires mean share without layer 2 q,k,v at most 0.40 but allows one book to drive the mean. Fix: require at least 4 of 5 books to show share without below share with, or below 0.40.

3. Sufficiency bar has no precision rule. With 5 books and a small denominator the mean 0.60 can be noisy. Fix: require the 95 percent interval for the layer 2 share to lie clearly above the layer 4 share, or pre register a maximum interval width.

4. Burn in accounting is unclear. The range 90,000 to 122,767 is exactly 32,768 tokens. Fix: state that the first 8,192 tokens are burn in and only the remainder is scored, consistent with the harness.

5. Training overlap check is not stated. The adapter trained on books 1260, 345, 37106 and 174 at tokens 40,960 to 47,103. Fix: confirm in the smoke run that the 5 measured segments avoid those book token ranges.

6. Propagation distance is not matched. Both interventions are local and upstream of layer 5, but layer 2 must pass through global layer 3 while layer 4 does not. Fix: keep layer 4 as the closest possible local control but state this path difference as a limit on specificity claims.

Quoted numbers match: 0.7971 [F113], 0.3816 [F138], and -0.05161 [F175] are cited with the correct share denominators.

Lab constraints:
Lab constraints (fixed facts about the setup, not results):
- Model: Muse Glimmer-30B, 52 decoder layers. Global layers (full attention, no position encoding): 3, 7, 11, ..., 51.
  All others are local (2,048-token sliding window, RoPE). A control in another layer should match the layer type.
- The tilt is measured over attention heads in layers 2 to 51. A change made in layer L directly changes layer L's own
  heads and can only change later layers. Layer 2's own heads carry a large part of the dial's change (C7 under the
  full dial: layer 2's heads -74 percent, layers 3 to 51 -13 percent), so a control placed in a later layer cannot
  reach them.
- A measurement uses a 32,768-token segment of a book, with an 8,192-token burn-in. The shortest of the 15 books has
  94,774 tokens, so a 32,768-token segment must start at or before token 62,006.
  Text already used (do not reuse it for a tilt measurement): the first 32,768 tokens of sets A (C5), B (C7) and C
  (C8); set A tokens 32,768 to 65,535 (C9); sets B and C tokens 60,000 to 68,191 (C6 and the exploratory probes);
  sets A and B tokens 70,000 to 78,191 (band-mute probe); sets B and C tokens 80,000 to 89,999 (behavior probe).
  The adapter trained on books 1260, 345, 37106 and 174 at tokens 40,960 to 47,103; never measure there.
  Unused text long enough for a segment: tokens 90,000 onward in the books that are long enough (each set A book has
  at least 173,244 tokens; check the others in the smoke run).
- Cost: one 32,768-token pass takes about 13.5 s; per book and condition, 9 passes (undriven, sham, 7 periods).
- Shares: say what the share is a share of. A share of layer 2 attention's change is not a share of the full dial.
- Heads are read at the input of each layer's o_proj. An adapter on o_proj changes only o_proj's output, after that
  read point, so switching it changes later layers' heads but never its own layer's heads (C9's review caught this).
- Already settled, do not re-propose: layer 2's v_proj is enough alone for about half of the dial (C8, set C) and
  needed for about half (C9, set A, against a same-layer gate control and a layer 4 v control).
- The C5 adapter has 32 modules in layers 2 to 5 (q, k, v, gate and o projections and the MLP's three), rank 8.

Critique:
1. Downstream denominator is small with no guard. The cited full change over layers 5 to 51 is -0.05161 [F175] on different text. A near zero per book full drop makes the share unstable. Fix: add a no call rule that requires a minimum full drop magnitude per book and overall, else result is inconclusive.

2. Necessity bar has no book level replication. Pass requires mean share without layer 2 q,k,v at most 0.40 but allows one book to drive the mean. Fix: require at least 4 of 5 books to show share without below share with, or below 0.40.

3. Sufficiency bar has no precision rule. With 5 books and a small denominator the mean 0.60 can be noisy. Fix: require the 95 percent interval for the layer 2 share to lie clearly above the layer 4 share, or pre register a maximum interval width.

4. Burn in accounting is unclear. The range 90,000 to 122,767 is exactly 32,768 tokens. Fix: state that the first 8,192 tokens are burn in and only the remainder is scored, consistent with the harness.

5. Training overlap check is not stated. The adapter trained on books 1260, 345, 37106 and 174 at tokens 40,960 to 47,103. Fix: confirm in the smoke run that the 5 measured segments avoid those book token ranges.

6. Propagation distance is not matched. Both interventions are local and upstream of layer 5, but layer 2 must pass through global layer 3 while layer 4 does not. Fix: keep layer 4 as the closest possible local control but state this path difference as a limit on specificity claims.

Quoted numbers match: 0.7971 [F113], 0.3816 [F138], and -0.05161 [F175] are cited with the correct share denominators.

Verdict: FIXABLE
